title: Fattoush Salad
subtitle: Lebanese bread salad with crispy flatbread croutons
excerpt: Fattoush is a Lebanese salad built from ripe tomatoes, cucumber, herbs and crispy fried or baked bread pieces. Sumac is the traditional souring agent; here red wine vinegar and lemon take its place with a similar bright, tangy effect.
sourceNotes: Fattoush is a Levantine bread salad with roots in rural Lebanese and Syrian kitchens where stale flatbread was refreshed in salad dressing. The word fattoush may derive from the Arabic fatteh, meaning crumbled bread.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the vegetables and dressing up to 2 hours ahead. Add the bread just before serving.

content.text: Traditional fattoush uses sumac for its fruity sourness. This version uses red wine vinegar and lemon as a straightforward substitute. If you can find sumac, dust it generously over the finished salad in place of some of the vinegar.
Make the flatbread croutons. Mix the flour with a pinch of salt and enough water to form a soft dough (about 60ml). Roll thin and cut into rough 3cm squares.
Fry the dough pieces in 2 tablespoons of the olive oil over a medium-high heat for 2 minutes per side until golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper and season with salt.
Whisk the remaining olive oil, red wine vinegar and lemon juice in a large bowl with salt and pepper.
Add the tomato, cucumber, pepper, spring onion, parsley and mint to the bowl. Toss to coat in the dressing.
Add the flatbread croutons right before serving so they are still crisp. Toss once and serve immediately.

items.symptom: Bread pieces are soggy by the time it reaches the table.
items.cause: Croutons were added too early and soaked up the dressing.
items.fix: Add croutons at the very last moment before serving.

items.cause: Tomatoes and cucumber released liquid after being cut.
items.fix: Salt and drain tomatoes and cucumber for 10 minutes first.
